14        On January 11, 2025, plaintiff Valeo Schalter und Sensoren GMBH (“Valeo”) filed an 
15   administrative motion to consider whether defendant NVIDIA Corporation’s (“NVIDIA”) 
16   material should be sealed.  Dkt. No. 192.  On January 17, 2025, NVIDIA filed a declaration in 
17   support of sealing pursuant to Local Rule 79-5(f)(3).  Dkt. No. 197.   
18        There is a strong presumption in favor of access by the public to judicial records and 
19   documents accompanying dispositive motions that can be overcome only by a showing of 
20   “compelling reasons supported by specific factual findings.”  Kamakana v. City & Cnty. of 
21   Honolulu, 447 F.3d 1172, 1178-79 (9th Cir. 2006) (cleaned up).  However, the presumption does 
22   not apply equally to a motion addressing matters that are only “tangentially related to the merits of 
23   a case.”  Ctr. for Auto Safety v. Chrysler Group, LLC, 809 F.3d 1092, 1101 (9th Cir. 2016).  A 
24   party seeking to seal documents or information in connection with such a motion must meet the 
25   lower “good cause” standard of Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(c).  Id. at 1098-99; Kamakana, 447 F.3d at 
26   1179-80.  The discovery matters at issue here do not address the merits of either party’s claims or 
27   defenses, so the Court applies the “good cause” standard of Rule 26(c). 
1   business information that, if revealed, could cause competitive harm to NVIDIA.  Dkt. No. 197 at 
2   2.  NVIDIA asserts that in particular many of the portions for which it seeks sealing reference “a 
3   confidential partnership that NVIDIA has not yet publicly announced.”  Id. at 3, 5-7.   
4        The Court agrees that good cause exists to seal the information NVIDIA has designated 
5   within these documents.  The redactions proposed to the public versions of these documents are 
6   minimal and narrowly tailored to address the concerns it identifies.  See Civil L.R. 79-5(c)(3).  The
